requirement:
When preparing the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, every terminology definition
referenced by the subject or any contributed source MUST contribute its complete
fenced declaration, including its phrase option. Definitions referenced by those
definitions MUST also be included transitively, without duplicates or
nontermination on cycles.

When an additional source read introduces a terminology dependency, the same
complete, transitive definition set MUST be supplied to the model and recorded
before accepting a submission.
rationale:
**Judgment:** the implementation and tests satisfy `requirements.definitions.authoring_inputs`. I found no unmarked implementation and no behavior outside the requirement.

**Mandatory set**
- `AssessmentSources::prepare` (`src/authoring/inputs.rs`) builds the selectors from:
  - the subject;
  - its `{cite}` requirements;
  - the `{impl}` and `{test}` sources;
  - the anchors.
- It then calls `definition_inputs` over those contributions plus the subject's own text (`Some(&subject.text)`).
- `definition_inputs` calls `terms::dependencies`. That function does the following:
  - `direct_references` collects `{term}` references from the subject text and from every contributed input. For Rust sources it scans comments, and for requirement globs it scans declaration bodies.
  - `close_dependencies` expands those references to a fixed point using a visited set. This handles cycles without repeated expansion or nontermination. It also reports unresolvable terms as errors.
- Each name becomes an `InputSelector::Definition`. It resolves to `target.raw_lines`, which is the full fenced declaration including the `:phrase:` option.
- Duplicates are removed twice: the `BTreeSet` removes repeated names, and `!mandatory.contains(&input)` removes repeats of identical inputs.

**Additional reads**
- `read` and `search` in `src/authoring/tools.rs` call `AssessmentSources::additional_definitions`. That function runs the same transitive closure over the newly delivered inputs, with no subject text. It filters out definitions already in the delivery or already recorded.
- The new definitions are attached to the tool result and added to `ToolDelivery.inputs`.
- In `assess` (`src/authoring/mod.rs`), pending inputs go to the model with the tool result. `record_inputs` records them, de-duplicated, as soon as the next response arrives. That happens before any `submit_judgment` is processed. So the supplied and recorded sets are complete before a submission is accepted.

**Tests**
- `bundle_combines_direct_references_terms_and_current_existing_selectors` checks the following:
  - It uses a cyclic pair of terms. The subject references only `unit`, and `value` arrives transitively.
  - Exactly 2 definition inputs are delivered, so there are no duplicates and the cycle terminates.
- `mandatory_git_inputs_require_staging_declarations_sources_and_terms` checks that a term referenced from source is included, and that an unstaged term file is reported.
- `definitions_introduced_by_a_read_are_supplied_and_recorded_before_submission` checks the following:
  - A read introduces `terms.value`, which transitively pulls in `terms.unit`.
  - Both are recorded exactly once, in the order `unit`, `value`.
  - Each record's text starts with `:::{definition}` and `:phrase:`.
  - The second request, the one that precedes the submission, contains the new definition text, and the first request does not.
- `reading_records_only_delivered_sources_and_their_terms` and `search_supplies_terminology_clamps_at_eof_and_reports_failures` check term delivery and recording for `habeas` and `ripgrep` reads. Together they cover line-range reads, EOF clamping, invalid arguments and parse failures.

**Minor gaps, none blocking**
- The unresolvable-term error path inside `prepare` has no dedicated test in these inputs. `close_dependencies` itself is exercised elsewhere, in `evidence.rs`.
- If one turn makes several tool calls, the same definition can appear in more than one tool result. It is still recorded once.

text: :::{req} authoring_inputs
When preparing the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, every terminology definition
referenced by the subject or any contributed source MUST contribute its complete
fenced declaration, including its phrase option. Definitions referenced by those
definitions MUST also be included transitively, without duplicates or
nontermination on cycles.
When an additional source read introduces a terminology dependency, the same
complete, transitive definition set MUST be supplied to the model and recorded
before accepting a submission.
:::{req} mandatory_inputs
The harness MUST construct each assessment's mandatory input set by combining
the contributions specified by the requirements applicable to that subject and
its inputs. A requirement that contributes inputs MUST cite this requirement and
define which sources it contributes and when. The harness MUST include every
applicable contribution, deduplicate identical selections, and report
unresolvable mandatory inputs before inference. The complete set MUST be supplied
in the initial model request.
Generated output under project-root `evidence/`, including symlink aliases, MUST
be omitted from mandatory inputs when the default exclusion applies. An explicit
workspace allow MUST permit those selections; an explicit disallow MUST abort
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial`.
:::{req} dependencies
Requirement and example evidence MUST include a definition input for every term referenced by its subject text or reviewed inputs.

Habeas MUST repeatedly include definitions referenced by required definitions until the set reaches a fixed point. Each required definition MUST have exactly one definition input per evidence record. Cyclic references MUST be permitted and MUST NOT cause repeated expansion or nontermination.
Validation MUST report missing required definition inputs and MUST NOT silently refresh snapshots.
